spec.concept: Pendulum period depends on length and gravity, but not on the mass; the formula T = 2π√(L/g) is the small-angle approximation.
spec.definition: A pendulum is a weight hung from a fixed point so that it can swing freely back and forth.

prediction.prompt: A 1-meter pendulum takes about 2 seconds per swing (there and back, small swings). How long does a 4-meter pendulum take?

extremes.watch: On the Moon, gravity is weaker, making the swing much slower.
Higher gravity pulls the bob back faster, shortening the period.

misconceptions.label: 4x the length, 4x the time
misconceptions.refutation: Swing time grows with the square root of length: 4x longer is only 2x slower.
misconceptions.source_note: Page states the correct model; that this mistake is common is unverified

misconceptions.label: Length barely matters
misconceptions.why_tempting: Swings seem to keep a steady beat, like a clock.
misconceptions.refutation: Length sets the beat: T = 2 pi sqrt(L/g), so a 4 m pendulum takes 4 s.
misconceptions.source_note: Page states the correct model; that this mistake is common is unverified
